column1: # None of `<`, `=` or `>` is an aontu operator, so a marker line is
# ordinary text: `<<<<<<< HEAD` parsed happily into the two-string list
# ["<<<<<<<","HEAD"] and an unresolved merge became a plausible DOCUMENT
# rather than an error. A file in that state is never what the author
# meant, so it is refused before the parse, with a code of its own.
# All three marker lines, alone and in the shape git actually leaves.
# The marker is reported wherever it sits, not only on line one.
# ... and what must NOT be refused. The run length and the line start are
# both load-bearing: a document may legitimately hold these characters,
# and refusing one that does would be a worse bug than the one being
# fixed. Each row below is a shape that LOOKS like a marker somewhere.
# Six is not seven, and eight is not seven.
# A marker must start the LINE: indented, it is a run of text again.
# Seven followed by something other than a space is not the git shape.
